listings.name: Banco do Brasil Cultural Centre
listings.content: A cultural centre with gallery, movie theatre, video room, library and stages; usually hosts the main exhibitions in town. An interesting building completed in 1906 with old-fashioned elevators/lifts.

listings.name: Casa França Brasil
listings.content: French cultural centre built in 1820, with gallery and video hall.

listings.name: City Hall
listings.content: Hosts the city council.

listings.name: Lapa Viaduct
listings.content: Colonial structure built in 1750 that brought water from springs to downtown.

listings.name: Municipal Theatre
listings.content: City Theatre, inspired by the Paris Opéra House.

listings.name: National Library
listings.content: The National Library offers guided tours on weekdays, showing visitors its rare collection, various bookstacks and the catalogue system. Registration with identification is required, and tours run for about an hour. They leave at 13:00 for English tours, and 11:00, 13:00 and 15:00 for Portuguese tours.

listings.name: Passeio Público
listings.content: Commissioned in 1779, this was to become the first public park in the Americas. Check out the original Rococo-style gate and the ironwork fountains.
listings.address: Rua Texeira de Freitas at Rua Mestre Valentim
listings.image: Passeio Público - Fonte dos Amores – Chafariz do Menino.jpg

listings.name: Petrobras Headquarters
listings.content: The headquarters for the federal gas (petrol) company is an interesting piece of brutalist architecture which somehow resembles a Rubik's Cube with some blocks missing.

listings.name: Praça da República
listings.content: Large park; good for a rest. Look for monkeys and capybaras that roam about.

listings.name: Sambódromo
listings.content: Site of the famous Carnaval parades, the Sambódromo is a long street flanked by grandstands and VIP boxes. From the start of the year until Carnaval week, technical rehearsals (Ensaios Técnicos) free to the public are held on Saturday and Sunday evenings, with 2-3 teams performing per session.
listings.address: Rua Marquês de Sapucaí - Praça Onze

listings.name: Selarón Steps
listings.content: A stairway covered by colorful tiles and the ever-evolving art work of Chilean artist Jorge Selarón.

listings.name: Estátua equestre de D. Pedro I
listings.image: Monumento a pedro i do brasil.jpg

listings.name: José Bonifácio Monument
listings.image: Jose Bonifacio (Rio de Janeiro, RJ, Brasil) .JPG

listings.name: Floriano Peixoto Monument
listings.image: Monumento a Floriano Peixoto, Cinelândia, cidade do Rio de Janeiro, Brasil.JPG

listings.name: Glória Inlet
listings.content: A beautiful spot for a stroll along the bank of Guanabara Bay.

listings.name: Memorial Monument of Opening Ports - Trade
listings.address: Rua do Russel/Praça Luiz de Camões, Glória
listings.image: Monumento Comemorativo da Abertura dos Portos - Comércio.jpg

listings.name: Valongo Wharf Archaeological Site
listings.content: The place where, during the first decades of the 19th century, ships carrying a total of almost a million African slaves landed. When slave trade was banned, freed slaves lived there for some time, eventually the whole area was entirely rebuilt and its dark history was forgotten until 2011, when African amulets and other items of worship were found during construction works. Nowadays the former wharf is an archaeological site and since 2017 a world heritage site.
listings.image: Cais do Valongo e da Imperatriz.jpg

listings.name: Campo de Santana
listings.content: It is near the site where Brazil was declared a Republic in 1889. It's also the site of the monument for Republican leader Benjamin Constant.

listings.name: Gloria Church
listings.content: Small but interesting church built in 1739. It is more correctly known as the Outeira da Gloria, outeira in Portuguese meaning “knoll” or small hill. The church was well sited to be seen by arriving sailors sailing into Guanabara Bay. The layout consists of two intertwined octagonal prisms. There are some interesting wooden engravings and tiles from Portugal. Best accessed by one of the world’s shortest funiculars from Rua do Russel. The ride is free. Nice views.

listings.name: Benedictine Monastery of Rio de Janeiro
listings.content: Colonial architecture. Founded in 1590.

listings.name: Candelária Church
listings.content: Neoclassic cathedral.

listings.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of Saint Sebastian
listings.content: A rather bizarre, modern cathedral shaped like a volcano, with a very impressively vacuous interior.
listings.image: Catedral de São Sebastião do Rio de Janeiro02.jpg

listings.name: Our Lady of Mount Carmel Church
Saint Paul Church
listings.image: Igreja de São Paulo em Santa Teresa, Rio de Janeiro, Brasil.jpg

listings.name: Church of São Francisco de Paula
listings.address: Largo de São Francisco de Paula, 9-11, Centro

listings.name: Church of Our Lady of Lapa
listings.image: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Lapa dos Mercadores Cúpula.jpg

listings.name: Church of Our Lady of Lampadosa
listings.image: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Lampadosa.jpg

listings.name: Church of St. Goncalo and St. George
listings.address: Rua Alfandega and Praça da República corner, Centro

listings.name: St. Francis Church
listings.address: Largo São Francisco da Prainha, Saúde

listings.name: Church of St. Francis of Penance
listings.content: Church of the Venerable Third Order of St. Francis of Penance is a part of the Convent of Saint Antony
listings.image: Convento de Santo Antônio - Igreja de São Francisco 04.jpg

listings.name: Church of Saint Lucia
listings.image: Saint Luzia Church, Rio de Janeiro.jpg

listings.name: Churches of Convent Carmo
listings.content: These churches were built in the 18th century as part of a Carmelite Convent. After the future Portuguese King John VI of Portugal arrived in Rio in 1808 the churches became the city’s former main cathedral and the royal chapel. It was the site of coronations, and royal weddings and funerals. it features baroque and rococo architecture, with an ornate gilded interior and intricate wood carvings, mainly by one of Rio's best Rococo wood carvers of the period, Inácio Ferreira Pinto.

listings.name: São Francisco da Penitência Church
listings.content: Colonial church built in 1773.

listings.name: Monastery of Saint Theresa
listings.content: Baroque

listings.name: Church Our Lady of La Salette
listings.content: Founded in 1914. It has neo Gothic arches. One of the most beautiful church in Rio de Janeiro.

listings.name: Museum of the Estate of Ceu
listings.content: An art and antique museum with a good collection of works by modern masters. During Carnaval 2006 some of its most famous works of art were stolen while a procession passed by outside.

listings.name: Image and Sound Museum
listings.content: For researchers about the Brazilian film, radio, and broadcasting industries.

listings.name: Museum of Modern Art
listings.content: After MASP in São Paulo, the second most important contemporary art museum in Brazil, (downtown, next to Santos Dumont airport). Modernist architecture on the edge of the Bay.
listings.image: MAM - Museu de Arte Moderna do Rio de Janeiro 02.jpg

listings.name: National History Museum
listings.content: A museum of Brazilian history stretching from colonial to imperial times; big collection of paintings, but poor in artifacts.

listings.name: Naval and Oceanographic Museum
listings.content: Installed in a building constructed in 1868, this museum preserves articles from the seafaring history of the city.

listings.name: National Museum of Fine Arts
listings.content: Another building modelled on one in Paris, this time the Louvre. Includes large paintings from Academicist and Neoclassical Brazilian artists, as well as many copies of European sculptures

listings.name: Rio Art Museum
listings.content: A museum opened in 2013 as part of the regeneration of the old port area. Made up of a new building with good views from the roof, next to a converted building that had been part of Rio’s former bus station. Rotating exhibitions changing annually.

listings.name: Tram Museum
listings.content: This small tram museum has photos of and artifacts from the glory days when trams were all over Rio, including some models of old tramcars and lots of electrical equipment.

listings.name: Museum of Tomorrow
listings.content: Forward-looking science museum in a compact but stunning Santiago Calatrava-designed building.
listings.price: R$30 adults, R$15 youth under 21, free for seniors 60+ or children under 6

listings.name: Military Museum Conde de Linhares
listings.content: Learn about the history of Brazil's military as you stroll through galleries with exhibits about historic conflicts and leaders. Large collection of military hardware including tanks, field artillery, and rocket launchers.

listings.name: Gustavo Capanema Palace
listings.content: Former ministry of culture, designed by French architect Le Corbusier; though small, it is regarded as an important pioneering work in modern architecture.

listings.name: Ilha Fiscal Palace
listings.content: The former Customs House for Rio has some fascinating decorations and is well worth the visit.

listings.name: Itamaraty Palace
listings.content: Former presidential palace (1889-1893) and foreign office; now hosts a museum of South American diplomacy, a library and the UN information offices in Brazil.

listings.name: Paço Imperial
listings.content: Old Imperial Palace built in 1743 (though impressively modest). Colonial architecture.

listings.name: Tiradentes Palace
listings.content: The seat of the Legislative Assembly, visitors are welcome to wander in the corridors along the perimeter of the first floor, which tell the history of the Legislative Assembly and the building (mostly in Portuguese). Access to the second floor can be arranged through a guided tour with volunteers at the reception.

listings.name: Artists' Open House
listings.content: Held over a few days in May and November of each year, when Santa Teresa's artists open their studios to the public. There are free shuttle buses from most parts of the city for this event.

listings.name: Mocidade Independente Samba School
listings.address: Rua Júlio do Carmo, 251 - Cidade Nova

listings.name: Samba City
listings.content: This arts and entertainment complex celebrates Carnaval year-round. Thursday nights at 20:00, there is a special Carnaval samba presentation called Forces of Nature (Forças da Natureza), which includes a dinner buffet, for R$190 per person, with students and senior citizens getting half-price.

listings.name: Santa Teresa Historic Tramway
listings.content: What was Brazil's only remaining metropolitan tramway, in continuous operation since 1859, ran from Largo da Carioca, across the Arcos da Lapa, and into Santa Teresa terminating at the Largo de Curvelo. The tramway was closed in 2014 after accidents, but as of October 2015 is running again. If you follow the road further up from the last stop, and take the second road to the left, after another 300 m you will reach a rest area with a nice viewpoint, from where you can see much of Rio.

listings.name: UFRJ School of Music
listings.content: A good place to catch free classical music concerts. Stop by during the day for a schedule or check the newspaper for events, as the surrounding neighborhood can be a bit shady at night.

listings.name: Bistrô do Paço
listings.content: Quick and quiet spot for a light lunch.

listings.name: Al-Kuwait
listings.content: A good place to try the Brazilian take on Middle Eastern food.

listings.name: Cafe Colombo
listings.content: Dates back to 1894 and has a dazzling tea room and arguably the best sweets and other delicacies in town.

listings.name: Pizzaria Guanabara
listings.content: Delivery service. - Other units: Avenida Ataulfo de Paiva, 1228 - Leblon. (+55 21 2294-0797), - Avenida Armando Lombardi, 75, Loja A - Barra da Tijuca, (+55 21 3153-4040).

listings.name: Olla Gourmet
listings.content: Buffet and cafe of salads, different meats, and desserts.

listings.name: Restaurante Nova Capela
listings.content: Try the house specialty of mutton with rice and broccoli (carneiro com arroz com brócolis).

listings.name: Pilão de Pedra Restaurant
listings.content: Another weigh & pay buffet that includes sushi.

listings.name: Restaurant Sobrenatural
listings.content: Has some of the freshest fish in Rio. Go on Monday, Wednesday or Friday, when they have live samba and chorinho music by renowned artists. Try their moqueca dishes. Air Conditioning.

listings.name: Ponto de Encontro Ximeninho
listings.content: Come here for some comfort Brazilian food, little fritters and feijoada and a Brahma to wash it down.

listings.name: Aprazível
listings.content: This restaurante mineiro, inside an antique villa, has nice veranda and garden seating with great views of Guanabara Bay. Reservations recommended.

listings.name: Espirito Santa
listings.content: Another fine restaurant in an old villa built in the 1930s, this eatery serves exotic dishes from the Amazon region, including fish such as piranha, and unusual fruits like cupuaçu, taperabá, and jambu. They also have a good selection of regional cachaças.

listings.name: Armazém São Thiago (Bar do Gomez)
listings.content: A beautifully restored former grocery store, with a high ceiling, nice wooden furnishings, and beer that's always ice-cold. Located a bit past where most tourists get off the tram, and frequented by an eclectic local crowd which spills out on to the sidewalk even in the afternoon.

listings.name: Bar Simplesmente
listings.content: Lively and popular with the young crowd. And not simply a bar; the food is inexpensive but good.
listings.address: Rua Pascoal Carlos Magno, 115 - Santa Teresa

listings.name: Beco do Rato
listings.content: This is in fact not a club but a street party. This place was a quite small and hidden beer and beverage deposit store. After a change in the administration it changed into a bar, offering good quality live music, and turned into one of the nicest street parties in Rio. Laid-back atmosphere typical of Rio, samba and beer. Is surrounded by historical buildings in this old forgotten spot of Lapa. On Tuesdays they have a "roda de samba" involving samba players sitting around a big table and people around singing and dancing. Nice day to go: get there early around 21:30. On Thursdays nights, chorinho is played (old style instrumental samba). Nice to see the old school players doing their best there, a bit of Buena Vista. On Fridays is the busiest day, with samba till 03:00.

listings.name: Goya Beira
listings.content: Pleasant little place for a drink or two, with a view of Praça Neves with the tram line. If you get hungry, try the pizza.

listings.name: Carioca da Gema
listings.content: Located in a nice old house from the 1900s, this place always has good samba groups playing. One of the best days is on Monday nights when on stage you can see one of the most powerful voices of samba, the singer Richah, with his group playing old Carnaval songs.

listings.name: Circo Voador
listings.content: Live music venue with plenty of live Carioca music.

listings.name: Clube Dos Democraticos
listings.content: Clube dos Democráticos was founded in 1867 and is one of the first carnaval groups of Rio. Nowadays the great ballroom of the beginning of the 20th century houses one of the best places to dance Brazilian rhythms, especially samba, in Rio. Best days are Wednesday and Thursday. Wednesday is the day of Forró (a Brazilian rhythm from Northeast really popular throughout the country) and on Thursday the traditional samba. Both days are awesome, if you're looking to experience a genuine Brazilian atmosphere where people dance all night long, even if you don't know any step of the ballroom samba, you'd be mostly invited to dance and taught by the locals. Inexpensive big beer bottles and caipirinhas.

listings.name: Rio Scenarium
listings.content: One of the most beautiful and best-known samba clubs in Rio de Janeiro. Was once elected by the British newspaper The Guardian as being one of the top 10 bars in the world. Nice decor, filled with antiques, paintings, medieval armors, old bicycles, etc., in an amazing 19th-century warehouse. Three floors: on the first floor the main stage, second floor is an annex where sometimes another band plays or there is a DJ playing mostly Brazilectro (mix of electronic music with Brazilian songs). Fridays and Saturdays are the busiest nights and sometimes specially in the summer there are pretty long lines, so get there early, around 22:00, to avoid them. Bring a valid ID/passport (copy is also accepted) to get in. By the entrance you get a consumption card (don't lose it!) and you pay your consumption and entrance fees at the cashier before leaving the building. Dress up.

listings.name: Sacadura 154
listings.content: Dance club.

listings.name: Pousada Favelinha
listings.content: Might be your choice if staying in a favela is your cup of tea.
listings.address: Rua Almirante Alexandrino 2023 - between Laranjeiras and Santa Teresa

listings.name: Casa MangoMango
listings.content: A bed & breakfast that offers nice prices for couples and groups. Great view, too!.
listings.price: From US$80, R$330-750 (US$130-280) per night in Carneval season

listings.name: ibis Rio de Janeiro Centro
listings.content: Three-star hotel. Rooms: 250.

listings.name: Hotel Inglês
listings.content: Nice location next to the park, but a bit overpriced compared to similar accommodation in the area.

listings.name: Casa Beleza
listings.content: Charming guest house in an exotic mansion with swimming pool and tropical gardens. The house was the former residence of the Governor of the State of Rio.
listings.price: Doubles from US$90, loft suite R$330, orange room R$280, blue room R$240 (2014)

listings.name: Maracanã Stadium
listings.content: Once the world's highest capacity football venue, it was able to hold nearly 200,000 people. In modern times, the capacity has been reduced because of safety considerations, and the introduction of seating for all fans. It is undergoing renovation, to expand it to hold 80,000. The matches of Rio's football clubs like Flamengo or Fluminense are usually far from full, so go along and watch a game. There is also a Soccer Museum inside.
listings.address: Av. Presidente Castelo Branco at Av. Maracanã

listings.name: Tijuca National Park
listings.content: A few km north of the beach, this mountainous subtropical forest is Brazil's smallest national park. It is largely hand-planted as much of the original forest was destroyed to make way for coffee plantations. Despite this it contains hundreds of species, many of which are threatened with extinction. Corcovado is to the east of the park but if you really want to appreciate what the park has to offer you have to drive along some windy, hilly roads and get out and hike. This sector of the park can be reached via Rua Boa Vista, and from São Conrado in Zona Oeste.
listings.address: Estrada da Cascatinha, 850 - Alto da Boa Vista

listings.name: Engenhão Stadium
listings.content: Estádio Olímpico João Havelange, known by its nickname of Engenhão, is a new soccer stadium built for the Pan-American Games of 2007. A modern construction, not as big as Maracanã but still worth a visit for soccer fans. The Botafogo team plays its matches there.
listings.address: Rua Arquias Cordeiro - Engenho de Dentro

listings.name: Grajaú State Park
listings.content: This 55-hectare park preserves some of the original forest and serves as a refuge for a wide range of species including marmosets, bush dogs, guinea pigs, parakeets, vultures, and hawks. The park includes the Pedra do Andaraí, symbol of the area.

listings.name: Museum of Astronomy and Related Sciences
listings.content: Also has an observatory.

listings.name: Museum of the First Reign
listings.content: A museum about the reign of Emperor Pedro I (1822-1831), but with a modest collection.

listings.name: Musical sidewalks of Vila Isabel
listings.content: The mosaic sidewalks along Boulevard 28 de Setembro between Praça Maracanã and Praça Barão de Drummond are musical staves. Written in the stones are 20 complete musical works, including tunes by Ary Barroso, Martinho da Vila, Almirante, Noel Rosa, and other famous Brazilian composers who frequented Vila Isabel back in its Bohemian heyday. If you know who these guys are, you might also be interested in checking out the famous sculpture of Noel Rosa on this street at the entrance to the bairro.

listings.name: Rio de Janeiro Zoo
listings.content: If you won't be making it to the Amazon or the Pantanal, this is a good place to see some of Brazil's more exotic creatures.
listings.address: Parque Quinta da Boa Vista - São Cristóvão

listings.name: Train Museum
listings.content: A modest collection of 19th-century engines, train cars used by emperors and presidents, and streetcars.
listings.address: Rua Arquias Cordeiro 1046 - Engenho de Dentro

listings.name: Museu do Açude
listings.content: The former residence of one of the founders of the Modern Art Museum, this museum hosts a collection of items from the history of Portuguese rule, including furniture, kitchenware, and an array of azulejos, or Portuguese blue tiles. There are also separate collections of Oriental art and Brazilian pop art.
listings.address: Estrada do Açude, 764 - Alto da Boa Vista

listings.name: Quinta da Boa Vista
listings.content: Park

listings.name: Church of Our Lady of Lourdes
Chapel of St. Roque
listings.address: Rua Padre Juvenal, s/n - Praça de São Roque - Ilha de Paquetá

listings.name: Church of the Good Lord Jesus of the Hill
listings.address: Praia dos Tamoios, 45 - Ilha de Paquetá
listings.image: Paquetá - Igreja Matriz do Senhor Bom Jesus do Monte - Exterior.jpg

listings.name: Convent of Our Lady of Help
listings.address: Praça Barão de Drumond, Vila Isabel

listings.name: Rock climbing
listings.content: Many climbers take on the 444-meter Pedra do Andaraí, in Grajaú State Park. See the See section for details.

listings.name: Ramos
listings.content: A popular, in-bay, beach where the government built an artificial pool on the sand (piscinão). This area is not recommended for foreigners to visit. Inappropriate for bathing.

listings.name: Unidos de Vila Isabel
listings.content: Founded in 1948, the city's fastest-growing samba school is now the third largest.

listings.name: Unidos da Tijuca
listings.content: Conceived in 1931.

listings.name: Adega Carne-de-Sol do Peixto
listings.content: As the name suggests they are best at carne-de-sol. They have a full menu of typical Brazilian food in good-sized helpings.

listings.name: Adegão Português
listings.content: This hole-in-the-wall joint has fantastic food that has attracted fans for over four decades. Lamb with vegetables and potatoes is a must-try.

listings.name: Fiorino Bar e Restaurante
listings.content: Good-quality Italian restaurant with reasonable prices. Note that they do not accept credit cards.

listings.name: Petisco da Vila
listings.content: This restaurant has for decades been the haunt of famous bohemian composers and poets such as Noel Rosa and Martinho da Vila. It remains the hotspot of Vila Isabel, with daily buffets, and feijoada on Saturdays. It also holds the distinction of having the highest annual draft beer sales of any restaurant in Brazil. Accepts Visa.

listings.name: Restaurante Quinta da Boa Vista
listings.content: Fine dining in what used to be the chapel for the Imperial Palace. The food is a fantastic display of traditional Brazilian cuisine with formal service.

listings.name: Restaurante Salete
listings.content: Famous for its shrimp risotto and empadinhas. Delivery available. Accepts credit cards.

listings.name: Pa Pa G
listings.content: Gay and lesbian nightclub.

listings.name: Barraco #55
listings.content: An arts and research centre and hostel at the same time in the middle of the favela Complexo do Alemão. Run by the friendly and helpful Dutch Ellen and her Brazilian partner, who will include you in the local life and culture festivals. Very authentic and enjoyable place to stay, different from the usual tourist life in Rio.
listings.address: Rua da Assembleia #19, Nova Brasilia, Complexo do Alemão

listings.name: Rio Aeroporto Hotel
listings.content: A good place to stay if you arrive late to Rio or are leaving early in the morning. Clean rooms with all the convenience of being within the airport. Rooms have no windows.
listings.address: inside Galeão International Airport, 3rd floor, Sector B

listings.name: Linx Hotel International Airport Galeão
listings.content: Only has 15 rooms for those who are stuck in the airport. Rooms have TV, telephone and air conditioning but no windows.
listings.address: Located in: RIOgaleão - Tom Jobim International Airport

listings.name: Aerospace Museum
listings.content: Good collection of planes, engines, etc. and a chance to see how Air Traffic Control works.

listings.name: Barra Woods
listings.content: This 560,000-m² park is one of the most visited green areas in the Zona Oeste, with a lake, walking trails through the woods, large lawns, playgrounds, and sporting facilities.
listings.address: Av. das Americas, km.6 - Barra da Tijuca

listings.name: Casa do Pontal Popular Art Museum
listings.content: The area's most important collection of popular arts and crafts.
listings.address: Estrada do Pontal 3295 - Recreio dos Bandeirantes

listings.name: Chico Mendes Ecological Park
listings.content: This 43-hectare park has walking trails through a preserved section of the Mata Atlântica (Atlantic Forest). They also offer a guided tour of the habitats of several local endangered species, including the three-toed sloth, the broad-snouted caiman, and the red-footed tortoise. There is an exhibit hall with exhibits on local wildlife.
listings.address: Avenida Jarbas de Carvalho 679 - Recreio dos Bandeirantes

listings.name: Pedra Branca State Park
listings.content: The largest ecological park in the city, and the largest urban forest in the world, with 12,500 hectares. Vegetation is typical of the old Atlantic forest, and fauna includes ocelots, sloths, armadillos, and toucans. Beyond the nature, there are also ruins of several structures, such as old farmhouses.

listings.name: Church of Our Lady of Loreto
listings.content: WEeest
listings.image: Igreja n s loreto jacarepagua rio.jpg

listings.name: Church of Our Lady of the Conception
listings.content: A modern church
listings.image: Igreja Nossa Senhora da Conceição Sta Cruz.jpg

listings.name: Cidade das Artes
listings.content: Large complex with cultural events at the heart of Barra.
listings.image: Cidade da musica city of music.jpg

listings.name: Sítio Roberto Burle Marx
listings.content: The garden of landscape architect and artist Roberto Burle Marx (1909-1994), with a collection of plants from all over Brazil. In 2021 it was listed as a world heritage site.

listings.name: Abricó beach
listings.content: Nudist beach. Facilities and telephone service are quite limited, so plan ahead.

listings.name: Pedra do Telégrafo
listings.content: Hike up this 354-m-high mountain and enjoy a beautiful view. Famous for the "cliffhanger images", which can be taken on top.

listings.name: Rio Water Planet
listings.content: A water park with over 40 attractions, located in Vargem Grande.

listings.name: Cabana do Pepe
listings.content: Pepe was a famous hang glider who passed away in a hang gliding accident in Japan a few years ago. He started a sandwich shop on the beach that makes a variety of healthy sandwiches. Especially good are the fruit smoothies. Not to be missed. Cabana do Pepe is run by Pepe's widow. This is the most popular area of the Barra beach, and is the best area for people watching.

listings.name: Alpendre
listings.content: Alpendre's menu is full of typical Brazilian cuisine from around the country.

listings.name: Beco do Alemão
listings.content: Although unexpected it is delightful. Germany food in Rio! Fantastic breakfast and salad bar.
listings.address: Avenida das Americas 1600 - Barra da Tijuca

listings.name: Caminho do Mar
listings.content: Excellent vegan option with three-course meals in a more lush quarter of Recreio. Offers pizza delivery on Saturdays. Prices can be a bit steep for locals.

listings.name: Rio/Brasa
listings.content: This churrascaria has unusually excellent meat and shrimp along with a salad bar and all the other standards of the genre. There is a monitored play area for children.
listings.address: Avenida Ayrton Senna 2541 - Barra da Tijuca

listings.name: Bar do Baiano
listings.content: Bar with a varied schedule of live music from Monday to Saturday, covering all types of music, from jazz to choro.

listings.name: Sugar Loaf Mountain
listings.content: One of the defining landmarks of the city. The cable cars take you up from for a breathtaking view of much of Zona Sul and the center, and also the city of Niteroi, just across Guanabara Bay. You have to queue again at Urca Hill (Morro da Urca) station for the second part of the ride. You can also walk up a trail to this point (start on Trilha do Morro da Urca along the shore, then climb the stairs on your left) and take the cable cars to Pão de Açucar and back to Praia Vermelha for R$92, or just back to Morro da Urca for R$59, or just down to Praia Vermelha for R$39 (full prices). This ticket office closes at 19:30, the downward trip is free after that. At Morro da Urca you can take a sightseeing helicopter trip, if you can afford it. The area is pretty secure, thanks to the various military institutions nearby. The buses number 511, 512, 591 and 592 and the subway buses from Botafogo bring you to the base station. Do not make the mistake of thinking you have seen enough once you have seen the view from Cristo Redentor. Try Sugarloaf at sunset for a truly mind-blowing experience. It is also possible to hike/climb up via the Escalada do Costão.

listings.name: Christ the Redeemer Statue (Corcovado peak)
listings.content: The 710 granite peak of Corcovado, capped by the famous 38-m statue of Jesus known as Christ the Redeemer (Cristo Redentor), has been the vantage point for countless picture postcards and travel posters through the ages. Its peak provides a sweeping panorama, from the interior of Guanabara Bay to the north, to Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas (Rodrigo de Freitas' Lagoon) to the south. Access to the mountain as a whole is free, but most of the good views are within the paid area of the Christ statue. You can't enter the statue itself except for a small chapel at the bottom of it.
listings.price: R$58 adults, R$32 children/students/seniors (included in price of some transportation)

listings.name: Arpoador
listings.content: The rocks at the Copacabana end of Ipanema beach. From here you can see a panorama including Corcovado and Sugar Loaf. It is supposed to be the best place to watch the sunset from in Rio. Reputedly a bit dangerous so go there at weekends when there are lots of people and a few police around.

listings.name: Guanabara Palace
listings.content: Former palace of the Imperial Princess, now the governor's office. Eclectic architecture. Not open to the public.

listings.name: Largo do Boticário
listings.content: A delightful square of well-preserved colonial style houses that date back to 1831.

listings.name: Laranjeiras Palace
listings.content: This is the official residence of the Governor of the State of the Rio de Janeiro

listings.name: Monumento a Estácio de Sá
listings.content: Erected in 1973. Homage to Estácio de Sá, the founder of Rio de Janeiro

listings.name: Basilica of the Immaculate Conception on the Botafogo Beach
Our Lady of the Rosary Parish Church
listings.address: 164, R. Gen. Ribeiro da Costa, Leme

listings.name: Church of Our Lady
listings.address: ~19, Rua Gago Coutinho, Rua das Laranjeiras, s/n°, Largo do Machado

listings.name: Casa das Canoas
listings.content: The former residence of architect Oscar Niemeyer. Call in advance.

listings.name: Museum of Folklore Edison Carrero
listings.content: Part of the National Centre for Folklore and Popular Culture (CNFCP). The museum was created in 1968 and today has around 13,000 objects by various authors, techniques and origins, kept in technical archives, available for consultation by institution-related post-graduate specialists, by appointment.

listings.name: Indian Museum
listings.content: Focusing on the history of Native Brazilians, with many artifacts including a home of the Umé culture. The gift shop has authentic handicrafts.

listings.name: Carmen Miranda Museum
listings.content: Here you'll find an amusing collection of photographs, posters, musical recordings, and, of course, gigantic fruity hats worn by the singing star. The building looks like an abandoned space capsule in the middle of the park.

listings.name: Army History Museum of Copacabana Fort
listings.price: Adults R$6, over 60 years old R$3, students with student ID R$3
listings.address: Praça Coronel Eugênio Franco, 1 - Posto 6 - Copacabana

listings.name: Museum of the Republic
listings.content: The former presidential palace (1893-1960) hosts a museum of recent history and nice gardens, with an adjacent art gallery and small theatre that occasionally shows free movies. One of main features is the room where president Getúlio Vargas shot himself in 1954.
listings.image: Palácio do Catete - Museu da República.jpg

listings.name: Museu Villa-Lobos
listings.content: Heitor Villa-Lobos wrote about 1000 pieces and is considered one of the world's greatest composers. This small collection includes a number of personal items, musical instruments, pictures and hand-written work by Villa-Lobos.

listings.name: Oi Futuro
listings.content: This former telephone museum hosts a fine gallery with temporary exhibitions of digital art or art with interactive medias; it is sponsored by the local phone company.

listings.name: Instituto Moreira Salles (IMS)
listings.content: Cultural Centre - at these days hosting a photo exhibition of the construction of Brasilia. Guided tours: Tu-F at 17:00.
listings.address: Rua Marques de São Vicente 476, Gavea

listings.name: Botanical Garden
listings.content: Planted in the 1800s, it is both a park and a scientific laboratory. It contains a huge collection of plants from all over the world, not only tropical ones. If you take the bus note that Jardim Botanico is also the name of a neighborhood and the road on which it is found so make sure you go all the way to the entrance. The gardens are well kept and very lush. Not far from the cafe, you are likely to hear swooshing sounds. Look up and you can see small monkeys swinging from tree to tree.
listings.image: Aleia Barbosa Rodrigues, no Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro - Brasil.jpg

listings.name: Parque Enrique Lage
listings.content: Public park with walking trails through subtropical forest. A cafe offers drinks and meals. A trail goes up to Corcovado mountain from here. The land was the residence of industrialist Enrique Lage and his wife, singer Gabriella Besanzoni. During the 1920s Lage had the mansion remodeled by Italian architect Mario Vodrel, with interior paintings by Salvador Payols Sabaté. The mansion was notably featured in the 2003 music video for Snoop Dogg's single "Beautiful."

listings.name: Flamengo Park
listings.content: 1.2 million m² with broad walkways, Flamengo Beach, various monuments, and over 10,000 trees. To its north is the Museum of Modern Art (see Centro).
listings.address: along the bay between Flamengo and Glória

listings.name: Hike/Climb Sugarloaf Mountain
listings.content: If you are keen on hiking and climbing up the full way, check out this trail. Equipment is needed as there is a vertical section with potentially serious consequences in case of a fall. If you do not have your own rock climbing equipment, go with a guide. On the way down you can use the gondola for free to get to Morro da Urca. From there, you can follow an easy trail to get back to the ground.

listings.name: Cláudio Coutinho Trail
listings.content: This pleasant walk follows the southern coast of Urca Hill (Morro da Urca), and side trails lead to various points on the hill, offering lush vegetation, monkeys, and nice views of the bay.

listings.name: Planetarium Espaço Museu do Universo
listings.content: There are shows, mainly for kids, in the planetarium on weekends. These are targeted at different age groups so it is essential to check the age the show you plan to attend is for or you may get stuck with one that is totally unsuitable. From Wednesday to Friday the space is also open without shows and there are around 60 hands-on scientific experiments to entertain kids.

listings.name: Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon
listings.content: A large lagoon in the middle of South Zone, with great views to Corcovado and Ipanema and Leblon beaches. You can run, walk, skate or cycle the 7.5 km around this freshwater lake and then retire to your luxurious Ipanema penthouse apartment, or just imagine it! Some have been known to swim in it although pollution levels are very high. Around Lagoa you can rent cycles, swan-shaped pedalos and, on the western side near where the helicopters take off, electric cars for younger kids.

listings.name: Pedalboats
listings.content: Pedal the lake in these swan-shaped boats for 2-5 people.
listings.address: on Lake Rodrigo de Freitas - Ipanema

listings.name: Quadracycle
listings.content: Take a ride around the lake on one of these unique contraptions, like a bicycle for two side-by-side riders under a little canopy.

listings.name: Hanggliding and Paragliding
listings.content: From the ramp atop Pedra Bonita, qualified instructors offer tandem flight courses in hang gliding, paragliding, and ultralight. Wind conditions are typically safe and offer splendid views of the surrounding beaches and mountains. Helicopter rides also available. Various clubs offer the experience: and [skycenter@skycenter.com.br.

listings.name: Panoramic helicopter rides
listings.content: These are noisy and drive Rio's residents mad as the helicopters circle the statue of Christ, but if you can live with that and can afford it, a helicopter trip is likely to be the most memorable experience of your visit to Rio. There are 2 operators in the city:Helisight: You can catch a copter at the first stage of the cable car ride up the Sugar Loaf or, alternatively, on the west edge of Lagoa. The basic trip takes in Sugar Loaf, Corcovado and Zona Sul (R$230 per person, minimum three people); longer, and more expensive, trips will take you to places such as the Maracana football stadium (R$350 per person). Prices quoted are web site prices. They may be negotiable on the day but no chance if a cruise ship is in town.Panoramic Flight RJ in Barra da Tijuca

listings.name: Helicopter Rider
listings.content: A helicopter ride over the beautiful beaches and over Sugarloaf Mountain and Christ the Redeemer.
listings.address: Av. Gen. Moisés Castelo Branco Filho, 700 - Golf Olímpico - Barra da Tijuca

listings.name: Pedra da Gávea
listings.content: Hike up this monolith of 844 m and enjoy one of the most spectacular city views in the world. It can be done either by booking a tour or on your own. The round trip takes roughly 4-5 hours and is strenuous and challenging with a stretch of light rock climbing ("Carrasqueira"). Bring enough water and food and wear proper shoes. Attention: There are stories online of people, who got robbed on the hike up.

listings.name: Hike up the Morro Dois Irmãos
listings.content: There are two viewpoints in this hike before reaching the final destination of the peak. From the first, you will be able to see Rocinha, which is the largest favela in Latin America, and a clear view of Pedra da Gávea. From the second, you are able to see Serra da Carioca, Gávea, Corcovado (where Christ the Redeemer stands tall), and Pedra Bonita. Once reaching the highest peak of the Morro Dois Irmãos you are able to see all of South Zone (Zona Sul) ranging from Botafogo to Leblon, including a beautiful view of Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon (Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas).

listings.name: Urca Beach
listings.content: Popular with the residents of Urca.

listings.name: Vermelha Beach
listings.content: The "red beach". Very safe due to military base, which is nearby.

listings.name: Leme Beach
listings.content: Somewhat less crowded than the Copacabana Beach

listings.name: Copacabana Beach
listings.content: Among the most famous beaches in the world, Copacabana attracts many tourists, both foreign and national. In summer, there are occasional free evening concerts of big name acts which draw huge crowds.

listings.name: Ipanema Beach
listings.content: The main beach for the middle-class, and specifically the Posto 9 section (watchtower #9) is preferred by left-wingers, intellectuals, artists, journalists and similar beach-goers. You can easily walk into a politician or someone famous here. The area close to the Farme de Amoedo street in Ipanema is known to attract the gay crowd of the city, who show off openly their sexuality.

listings.name: São Conrado Beach
listings.content: On the other side of the Dois Irmãos mountain west of Leblon, this beach is popular with middle class people and favela dwellers alike. Good surfing and hang-gliding opportunities. Sometimes inappropriate for bathing. The south zone can be seen through a helicopter ride where you can marvel at the magnificent view of the most beautiful beaches in the capital of Rio de Janeiro, as well as flying over monuments such as Sugarloaf Mountain and Christ the Redeemer.

listings.name: Cervantes
listings.content: The menu is composed by big sandwiches, with whatever you want: ham, salami, cheese, tenderloin and so on, with one home special ingredient: a big pineapple slice. It's a tropical taste to the end of your night. Famous for making their classic filet mignon and pineapple sandwich in the blink of an eye. Look out for the legendary "Penguin Waiter", who've been working there forever. You won't have a problem to find out who he is.

listings.name: Galeria Condor
listings.content: This two-story shopping arcade has a number of inexpensive Middle Eastern restaurants on the ground floor.

listings.name: Le Bistrôt Du Cuisinier
listings.content: Some fine Parisian cuts here, roast duck, whatever you like.

listings.name: Berbigão
listings.content: Seafood restaurant with good selection.

listings.name: Cantina Donanna
listings.content: Italian cuisine.

listings.name: Casa da Feijoada
listings.content: Serves nothing but traditional, authentic Brazilian feijoada.

listings.name: Filé de Ouro
listings.content: A good alternative to churrascarias, this steakhouse is simple and cozy. During the weekends there are usually big lines, but the steak is delicious. Try Filé à Oswaldo Aranha, with toasted garlic.

listings.name: Gula Gula
listings.content: A trendy restaurant with excellent salads, main dishes and desserts.

listings.name: Carretão
listings.content: Good-value rodizio – all-you-can-eat salad and barbecue.

listings.name: Nam Thai
listings.content: Fairly authentic and very popular Thai restaurant. Reservations essential at weekends.

listings.name: New Natural
listings.content: A good per-kilo restaurant. It is attached to a whole foods shop and has a good buffet selection, including sushi.

listings.name: Via Sete
listings.content: This grill restaurant offers a great bang for the buck: from their veranda you get to people-watch pretty Brazilians. There you can enjoy tasty wraps and sandwiches.

listings.name: Manekineko Leblon
listings.content: Sushi.

listings.name: Marius Carnes
listings.content: One of the best churrascaria in town.

listings.name: Viva Gastronomia
listings.content: Very good all-you-can-eat rodizio.
listings.address: Av. Nossa Senhora de Copacabana, 796 - Copacabana

listings.name: Zazá Bistrô Tropical
listings.content: A trendy, sexy and exotic place with great South Asian dishes. Good to go as a couple.

listings.name: Academia da Cachaça
listings.content: With over 500 varieties, this is the place to start your studies of Brazil's national drink.

listings.name: Bip Bip
listings.content: This unpretentious and thoroughly un-touristy hole-in-the-wall botequim has been a favorite hang-out of top local musicians for decades and hosts regular live choro, samba, and bossanova performances.

listings.name: Empório
listings.content: Popular with the younger crowd, that hangs out there to listen to DJs playing rock. Most of the crowd hangs out there because they are underage and can't get in the underground nightclubs. Gets packed with foreigners during summer.

listings.name: Garota de Ipanema
listings.content: There's no better place in Rio, Brazil, or even the world to watch bathing beauties stroll by than this cafe-bar, named after the song which according to legend was written here in 1962.
listings.address: Rua Vinicius de Moraes and Rua Prudente de Morais - Ipanema

listings.name: Mamma Jamma Pizzeria Rústica
listings.content: Pizza and draft beer is the name of the game here, though good quality. And save room for dulce de leche.

listings.name: Casa da Matriz
listings.content: Nightclub.

listings.name: Fosfobox
listings.content: "Fosfo" as it's nicknamed by the goers has a strong Saturday rock-oriented party. Young, trendy crowd with djs playing mostly indie rock, discopunk and electro-rock. After 04:00 it has a more electronic after-party. Different parties happen on Fridays, but it's usually electronic, with favorite genres being electro, house and minimal. Other nights are usually more electronic also, but has had Rock parties also on Thursdays. On Tuesdays there's a dub/reggaeton party.

listings.name: Cariocando
listings.content: A fairly new establishment, offering a bit of Lapa in the Zona Sul. Live music (samba, choro, MPB) Tu-Su. They seem to have a knack for booking the lesser-known offspring and siblings of more famous musicians.

listings.name: Bar do Tom
listings.content: Hosts lesser names, mainly performing Brazilian music.

listings.name: Sala Cecilia Meireles
listings.content: The city's main venue for classical performances.

listings.name: Ace Hostel
listings.content: Basic accommodations in large dormitories. Fabulous breakfast buffet. Excellent value. Right at the beach of Botafogo.

listings.name: Arpoador Inn
listings.content: Clean place, older interior, only a sidewalk apart from the beach.

listings.name: Beija Flor
listings.content: Typical budget hotel in Catete district. The rooms have no exterior windows and just open into the hallway, so take a look before deciding.

listings.name: CabanaCopa Hostel
listings.content: A, unique hostel in the safest part of Copacabana. A large colonial house, fully renovated with spacious ensuite dorms, excellent social areas, great breakfast and friendly, helpful staff.

listings.name: Che Lagarto Hostel Copacabana
listings.content: One of the most popular backpackers spots in Copacabana with engrossing New Year's and Carnaval events and a bar next door featuring live music. Big, airy rooms and great common areas, staffed by very knowledgeable, cool young people.

listings.name: Che Lagarto Hostel Ipanema
listings.content: Has both private and shared rooms. It is located one block away from the beach. You have access to Wi-Fi, a public kitchen and the bar. The breakfast is included.

listings.name: Rio Copa Hostel
listings.content: Free pickup from the airport, breakfast.

listings.name: Ferreira Viana
listings.content: As long as you don't mind climbing three flights of stairs (no elevator), this is as good a value as any among the budget hotels in the area, with friendly service.

listings.name: Jucati
listings.content: Well equipped apartments with free internet Wi-Fi available.

listings.name: Riazor
listings.content: Excellent location and cheap, but the rooms could be nicer.

listings.name: Terasse Hostel
listings.price: R$40 in dormitory, R$140 for a couple.

listings.name: Astoria Copacabana Hotel
listings.content: Good mid-range hotel. Not to be confused with the more upscale Astoria Palace (below), operated by the same owners.

listings.name: Rio Design Hotel
listings.content: This calls itself a Design Hotel. Each floor has a different style of suites that is really what distinguishes this locality. Top floor restaurant for breakfast and a good view of local favelas.

listings.name: Rio Guesthouse
listings.content: A boutique guest house on the beachfront, in a 1200-m² penthouse. Beautifully decorated, very comfortable.

listings.name: Hotel Vermont
listings.content: Affiliated with the nearby San Marco Hotel and Hotel Carlton in Leblon. Very friendly and helpful service.

listings.name: Rio INN Art
listings.content: The Suites has two types of rooms: Private and Private Low Cost. It is 4 blocks away from the beach.

listings.name: Che Lagarto Suites Copacabana Santa Clara
listings.content: The Suites has two types of rooms: Private and Private Low Cost. Breakfast, public kitchen and Wi-Fi included.

listings.name: Astoria Palace Hotel
listings.content: Fantastic rooftop pool with a great view of the beach.

listings.name: Belmond Copacabana Palace
listings.content: An iconic hotel dating to 1923, with a history of hosting the famous and wealthy. Arguably the best hotel in Rio.

listings.name: Copacabana Praia Hotel
listings.content: Four-star hotel. Services: pool, restaurant, sauna, Wi-Fi, IDD telephone, safety deposit box, air conditioning, room service, outdoor pool, minibar, laundry, LCD TV, bar.

listings.name: JW Marriott Hotel Rio de Janeiro
listings.image: JW Marriott Hotel Rio de Janeiro 2.jpg

listings.name: Sheraton Rio Hotel & Resort
listings.content: The only hotel in the Zona Sul with direct beach access.

places.blurb: Teatro Carlos Gomes is a theatre in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
